q: Alto Adige's signature native white, planted around Termeno/Tramin, is:
exp: Though Pinot Grigio/Bianco and Schiava dominate acreage; Lagrein is the dark native red.

q: Which DOCG sparkling of Piedmont is red, frothy and sweet, from Brachetto?
exp: Rose-scented red fizz; Moscato d'Asti's crimson cousin.

q: Timorasso, revived by Walter Massa, comes from which Piedmont hills?
ans: Colli Tortonesi (Derthona is the label term)
exp: Waxy, mineral, age-worthy — Piedmont's white answer to Burgundy pretensions.

q: Barolo Riserva may not be released until how long after the harvest?
exp: Sixty-two months, counted from 1 November of the harvest year, so a 2016 Riserva reaches the market in 2022. Straight Barolo needs 38 months with at least 18 in wood; Barbaresco needs 26 months with 9 in wood, and Barbaresco Riserva 50. The wood minimum matters historically: until the 2010 revision Barolo demanded two years in cask, and its reduction to 18 months was part of the settlement that ended the Barolo Wars, legitimising shorter barrique regimes without forcing anyone off large botti.

q: Give the grape composition Amarone della Valpolicella requires, including the Corvinone clause.
accept: corvina 45 to 95 percent with corvinone replacing up to half plus rondinella 5 to 30
corvina and corvinone with rondinella and molinara now optional
45 to 95 corvina 5 to 30 rondinella up to 25 percent others
corvina up to half of it corvinone rondinella and a small balance of others
ans: Corvina 45-95%, of which up to half may be replaced by Corvinone; Rondinella 5-30%; and up to 25% other permitted non-aromatic red varieties, no single one of them exceeding 10%. Molinara has been optional since 2003
exp: Corvinone was long assumed a Corvina clone and is in fact a distinct variety — larger berries on looser bunches, later ripening, which is precisely why it dries cleanly in the fruttaio and why growers use the substitution clause. Molinara's demotion from mandatory in 2003 removed a pale, high-acid, low-colour component that many felt thinned the wine; a few traditionalists still insist on it. The same composition rules govern Valpolicella, Ripasso and Recioto, so one answer serves the whole pyramid.

q: Vin Jaune must age in cask sans ouillage a minimum of how long before bottling in clavelin — and how many of those months must be under voile?
ans: Six years and three months (60 months under voile minimum)
exp: No topping up; the veil of yeast protects and transforms.

q: Why does the clavelin hold exactly 62 cl?
accept: what remains of a liter after aging
the share lost to the angels
ans: Legend: what survives of a liter after six-plus years of evaporation
exp: The only bottle size permitted for Vin Jaune.

q: Château-Chalon's status is unusual because the AOP covers:
exp: Château-Chalon = Vin Jaune exclusively; in weak years the whole appellation may be declared off.

q: Name the Jura's two indigenous red grapes beside Pinot Noir.
exp: Poulsard: rose-pale, ethereal; Trousseau: darker, peppery — Bartolo of the mountains.

q: What distinguishes 'ouillé' Jura whites from traditional ones?
ans: Barrels are topped up (ouillage), preventing the oxidative voile — fresh 'floral' style
exp: The modern Jura split: ouillé purity vs sous-voile tradition.

q: Macvin du Jura combines unfermented juice with:
ans: Marc du Jura (pomace brandy) — a mistelle
exp: Cousin to Pineau des Charentes and Floc de Gascogne.

q: Savoie's Chignin-Bergeron cru is dedicated to which grape under its local name?
exp: The alpine exception to Jacquère's reign; apricot and mountain herbs.

q: Which Savoie red grape gives peppery, violet alpine wines in Arbin?
exp: Syrah's structural cousin; Arbin is its stronghold.

q: Corsica's Sciacarello thrives on which rock around Ajaccio?
exp: Granite west (Sciacarello); schist north (Nielluccio's Patrimonio is the limestone pocket).

q: Muscat du Cap Corse is fortified from which Muscat?
exp: The island's VDN; Rappu is the rarer red counterpart.

q: Domaine de la Pinte and Overnoy/Houillon anchor which Jura commune's natural-wine fame?
exp: Pierre Overnoy bottled sans soufre from 1984 — the movement's touchstone.
